title: Spectrality for quasi-compact algebraic stacks with quasi-compact diagonal
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose $\mathcal X$ admits a smooth surjective atlas by a quasi-compact scheme and its diagonal $\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact, with the chart conventions of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Give $|\mathcal X|$ the field-valued point set and smooth-atlas topology of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]. Then $|\mathcal X|$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]: it is quasi-compact, every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point, its quasi-compact open subsets form a basis, and the intersection of two such opens is quasi-compact. In particular it is Kolmogorov (any two distinct points are distinguished by an open subset) and quasi-compact. No finite-type, Noetherian or separation hypothesis on the diagonal is imposed.

proof.text: Set $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$. A field is a commutative ring by [def-weil-field], so $S$ is an affine scheme by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The given quasi-compact smooth surjective atlas says precisely that $\mathcal X$ is quasi-compact by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. The relative diagonal over $S$ is exactly the diagonal $\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ in the hypothesis; no change from a relative to an absolute diagonal is made.

source.place: Tag 0DQN, lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc; specialization of the existing affine-base node to Spec k.

proof.text: Apply the existing general result [lem-sfb-qc-stack-spectral-point-space] with the affine base $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ from step 1. Its quasi-compactness and relative-diagonal hypotheses are exactly those just checked. Its point set is the same field-valued point set, with the same equivalence after common field extension, and its topology is the quotient topology for a smooth surjective scheme atlas. This is precisely the topology in [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets]: both topology descriptions characterize a closed subset by closedness of its inverse image in the same atlas, as also stated in [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. Thus the conclusion applies to the specified space itself. It gives quasi-compactness, a basis of quasi-compact opens stable under finite intersections, and a unique generic point for every nonempty irreducible closed subset. These are all the spectrality clauses of the item. The existing result explicitly imposes none of the additional finite-type, Noetherian or separation conditions excluded here.

source.place: Tag 0DQN, lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc; specialization of the existing affine-base node to Spec k.

proof.text: For completeness derive the Kolmogorov assertion from sobriety in [def-weil-spectral-space]. If $x,y$ lie in exactly the same opens, they lie in exactly the same closed subsets, so $\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}$. The closure of a singleton is nonempty irreducible: if it is contained in the union of two closed sets, the singleton lies in one of them and hence its whole closure lies there. Both $x$ and $y$ are generic points of that closed set. Uniqueness of the generic point, supplied by step 2, forces $x=y$. Hence distinct points are distinguished by an open. Quasi-compactness has already been obtained in step 2. For the empty stack the same conclusions hold vacuously, with the empty space quasi-compact.
